terms.comment: The term of modern grammars for the verbal adjective in -ndus: legendōrum librōrum causā (Traupman 235). Lewis & Short gives gerundīvus modus only from Servius, and as a name for the gerund; we have found no ancient instance of gerundīvum for the gerundive.

phrases.latin: Gerundīvum quid est? — Est adjectīvum verbāle.
phrases.english: What is a gerundive? — It is a verbal adjective.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 235, 246.
